$comment: Gemfall beat 1, The Spark. Story: docs/campaigns/gemfall.md §1. Wiring: docs/campaigns/gemfall-authoring.md. Must set on every path to every ending: exactly one motive_* (choice_why_north, which every path passes through) and exactly one of ember_sold / ember_kept (choice_ember, which every path passes through). The six motive votes each land on a short result scene (scene_motive_*) before the docks, so the vote is seen to matter at the table. Mostly people, prices and promises, with one gentle fight on the spine: two wisps drawn to the warm Ember Facet tangle the quay lamps (scene_quay_wisps, encounter_quay_wisps), which every road walks between the tavern and Madame Fenn; a lost fight is a cocoa rescue that rejoins at choice_ember, never a setback. Expansion: the prologue ends on a vote (what the party was doing on the docks that night), and each pick pays off later in the chapter: the lamps open Old Wick's path over the Long Bridge, the oranges buy the sailors' rumors, the sardine feeds the gull. Further episodes: the jammed Long Bridge, the Griffin Post (whose friends can vouch for the stone), the gull, Mrs. Tuft's provision barge, Mortar's goodbye (whose word gets you hired by Hesper), and the North Gate on the way out. Second pass: a selkie family arriving on the quay (help them, and they make room for you when the Empty Chair inn is full) and the full inn itself. Interactions on the spine: the pear line (relay), the letters (timing), Mrs. Tuft's jar tray (balance) and the lantern pole (cooperate).
title: The City That Smelled Opportunity

objectives.label: Listened to the scholar everyone laughed at
Heard the rumors of all three roads north
Signed on as real caravan crew

goal.text: Get ready for the long trip north.

steps.label: Find a bed for the night

facet_ember.name: The Ember Facet
facet_ember.text: A red stone, warm as toast, that fell from the sky into an Exchange gutter by your boot.

scene_prologue_realm.narration: This is the Realm of Red Sky. Far to the north stands Mount Red Sky. Old maps say it is only sleeping. Tonight your story begins at the Exchange docks. Your job: get ready for the long trip north.

scene_prologue_city.narration: The Exchange is a city where roads and rivers meet the sea. People come here to trade and to start again. Nobody is from here. That is the whole point.

scene_prologue_party.narration: You met on the docks this week. Together you have six coins and one supper bundle. The harbor lamps are coming on. What are you doing tonight?

scene_prologue_party_prologue_begin.narration: You catch two old boots and one silver sardine. You keep the sardine. A gull stares at it. The sardine stares back.

scene_prologue_party_oranges.narration: You help a yeti captain unload his orange ship, the Sunny Disposition. He has peel in his fur. "We owe you one," he says. "Mostly in oranges."

scene_prologue_party_lamps.narration: Old Wick, a frogfolk lamplighter, says goodnight to every lamp by name. You carry his ladder. He shows you a secret ledge along the Long Bridge. "Nobody else looks."

scene_prologue_party_cards.narration: Your kitsune does card tricks. A sailor's card turns up in his boot, then his hat, then his sandwich. He laughs and gives you his lucky stone, a pebble with a hole in it.

scene_red_sky.narration: The northern sky turns cherry red. Gem-light rains down far away. For a blink, some of it falls up. A gull drops its fish. Both look surprised.

scene_lighthouse.narration: From the lighthouse, you see one thread of gem-light rise toward the mountain. The old merfolk keeper sits up in her bathtub. "I saw nothing," she says. Neither did you.

scene_harbour_wall.narration: Every ship swings around until its nose points north. The tower bells ring, then stop. Nobody knows why. The lighthouse lamp shuts one eye.

scene_night_docks.narration: A boy changes his rope price. A fishmonger looks north and doubles the herring price. "Rush prices!" somebody shouts.

choices.label: Sit on a crate and watch

scene_stampede.narration: Three days later, the Exchange is packed with gem hunters. Prices go up while you read them. Before you go north, you need a reason, road news, food, a bed and a caravan. First, find somewhere to talk.

scene_plaques.narration: Seventeen brass plaques name seventeen different founders. One just says MY GRANDMA. A centaur tour guide says it means everybody belongs here.

scene_long_bridge.narration: The best place to talk is a noodle stall across the Long Bridge. But the bridge is jammed. A goat is standing on a merchant, who has not noticed. Below, a cabbage barge floats by.

check_bridge_squeeze.prompt: Wriggle across a bridge where nobody can move

onSuccess.narration: You go sideways, then under a cart, then over a very patient yeti, and pop out of the far end like a cork from a bottle. The noodle stall is right there.

onFailure.narration: The crowd swallows you up and carries you the whole way across without your feet touching the ground once. It sets you down very politely, facing the wrong way, right beside the noodle stall.

scene_long_bridge_barge.narration: You float under the bridge, past hundreds of dangling feet. You arrive by the noodle stall smelling of cabbage.

scene_long_bridge_lamp_path.narration: Old Wick's ledge is empty, just as he said. Halfway across, there he is, lighting a lamp at noon, just to be sure. He tips his hat.

scene_long_bridge_wade.narration: Your bigfoot wades into the canal. Everybody climbs onto their shoulders. Then two strangers. Then the goat. The whole bridge cheers.

choice_why_north.narration: At the noodle stall, a stone troll named Mortar points at an empty chair. "Every table keeps one for whoever comes next. Today, that is you." So, why are you going north?

scene_motive_wealth.narration: Mortar chalks RUSH PRICES on his board. Your noodles are free. Three pickpockets scoot one table closer.

scene_motive_curiosity.narration: Mortar stops stirring. "The gull dropped its fish before the light came. Heard something first." He has thought about that for three days.

scene_motive_prestige.narration: Mortar writes your names on his board under TODAY'S HEROES. He spells one wrong. A faun asks you to sign her dumpling.

scene_motive_duty.narration: Mortar sets out an extra bowl "for whoever needs it." A lost faun gobbles it up, spots her cousins' wagon, and runs after it with the spoon.

scene_motive_fresh_start.narration: Mortar taps your chair. "Yours now. Everyone here started again." He gives you bread. At rush prices, that is practically a house.

scene_motive_proving.narration: Mortar points at the Big Bowl. "Nobody finishes it." You finish it together. "Hm," says Mortar. From a troll, that is clapping.

scene_newcomers.narration: On the way to the docks, a selkie family steps off a boat with everything they own. "Is there room here for selkies?" asks the grandmother. "We were told to try the Empty Chair, an inn up the hill."

choices.label: Carry their bags to the inn
Risk lifting it all at once

check_newcomers_carry.prompt: Carry a whole family's luggage up the busiest street in the realm

onSuccess.narration: Trunks, bundles, a rocking chair and a fishbowl with a very calm fish in it: you carry the lot up the hill without dropping a thing. The selkies take a room at the Empty Chair, and the five children wave from the window until you turn the corner.

onFailure.narration: Halfway up the hill the biggest trunk pops open, and out pour about a hundred knitted socks. All five children help you chase them down the street. It takes ages, and it is the most fun anybody has had all week. The selkies take a room at the Empty Chair, socks and all.

scene_newcomers_plaque.narration: You find a plaque with a selkie founder on it. The grandmother reads it twice. "Then we are home." She gives you her river charm for the road.

scene_newcomers_fresh.narration: You swap fresh-start tips: eat at Mortar's and ignore the prices. The selkies head for the Empty Chair and promise to save you some room.

scene_docks.narration: At the docks, everybody trades news, and you need to know the roads north. A boggart in a coat made of coats sells "slightly used rumors." A yeti fishmonger shouts road news between herring prices.

scene_docks_sailors.narration: The crew of the Sunny Disposition cheer when they see you. Sailors pay their debt in rumors, one from every port, and an orange each.

check_rumours.prompt: Catch three good rumors out of a whole dock shouting at once

onSuccess.narration: You stand very still in the middle of all that shouting and pick out the good bits: one from a sailor, one from a drover, one from a frogfolk with reeds in her hat. Three rumors, three roads, caught like fish in a net.

onFailure.narration: The dock shouts too fast. You catch half a rumor about a pie and a whole one about somebody's aunt. In the end the yeti fishmonger takes pity on you and says the roads again, slowly, between herrings.

scene_boggart.narration: The boggart sells rumors in jars. You pay with a button. The rumor inside is: "The mountain is grumpy." Then the boggart says it again, slowly, looking west toward the marshes.

scene_three_rumours.narration: There are three roads north. East to Stone Crossing, where the toll is a story. North across the Plains, with the rush wagons. West through the Whispering Marsh, if the frogfolk like you. The fishmonger points up. "Griffin couriers carry so many letters, they can barely fly."

scene_griffin_post.narration: In the market stands the Griffin Post, a tower full of round windows. Clerks stuff more and more letters into the couriers' sacks. The postmaster, a griffin called Quill, has lost count. "Hands!" she squawks. "Anybody with hands!"

check_post_sort.prompt: Sort nine hundred claim letters before the griffins take off

onSuccess.narration: You sort them by mountain, then by valley, then by how loud the handwriting is. Postmaster Quill is so pleased she gives you a brave whistle, the kind couriers blow to clear the sky.

onFailure.narration: You sort the letters beautifully, into all the wrong sacks. A letter for a duke is now going to a duck. Quill sighs, says it will all come out in the wash, and stuffs everything into one enormous sack anyway.

scene_griffin_post_feed.narration: The couriers have not eaten since the red night. One young griffin swallows a whole loaf in one gulp, then bows with his wings out. In griffin, that means: I will remember you.

scene_griffin_post_shop.narration: Your griffin and the couriers talk about headwinds. Then they whisper. Since the red night, no courier flies near the mountain. "The air up there hums," says one, "like a kettle."

scene_gutter_glint.narration: Overhead, a courier's sack splits. Letters flutter over the market. Plink! A warm red stone lands by your boot. It is plum-sized, and it glitters, and it hums.

scene_gutter_glint_griffin.narration: A courier you know lands on a chimney and peers at the stone. "Not mine. That fell out of the sky." He fluffs his feathers. "Finders keepers!"

scene_nobody_claims.narration: Eleven people say it is theirs. None of them can say what color it is. The stone is yours, for now.

scene_gull_dive.narration: On the way up to the Empty Chair, a gull lands in front of you. It looks like the gull from the red night. It stares at your pocket, and crouches to dive.

check_gull_grab.prompt: Catch a seagull in mid-dive, gently

onSuccess.narration: You catch the gull in mid-dive, very gently, like a loaf of bread. It looks embarrassed. You set it down on a post, and it pretends that was where it was going all along.

onFailure.narration: The gull is quicker. It snatches the stone, flaps three circles over the market, finds it is much heavier than a fish, and drops it down the chimney of the nearest tavern. You run in after it and fish it out of the ashes, still warm, and only a little sooty.

scene_gull_dive_bread.narration: The gull takes your supper, cloth and all, and leaves the stone alone. Your tummies rumble all the way to the Empty Chair.

scene_gull_dive_sardine.narration: The gull gulps the sardine. Then it follows you to the Empty Chair like a small, very loud guard.

scene_gull_dive_outfly.narration: Wings out, up you go! The gull has never been chased by anything bigger than a cat. It leaves in a hurry.

scene_tavern.narration: Inside the Empty Chair, a selkie scholar stands on a table. "The gem-light fell upward!" Everyone laughs. Two trolls carry her outside, table and all. She just wants someone to believe her.

scene_scholar_believed.narration: The scholar hugs you. It is a very wet hug, because she is a selkie. "Professor Marrow Tidewell," she says. "You are the first to believe me all week!" She gives you the owl-feather clasp from her coat.

scene_scholar_theory.narration: Outside, the scholar draws a gem with eight sides on a napkin. Her soggy notes are signed Professor Tidewell. "Old stories tell of a seal, like a lid on a jar, made of eight pieces called facets," she says. "I think the mountain just threw seven of them across the realm. The eighth is still inside." She looks at your glowing pocket. "Oh! You've got one."

choice_ember.narration: Along the quay, gem-buyers shout prices. The loudest is Madame Coralie Fenn, a merfolk in a barrel on wheels. "Rush prices, darlings!" She offers a huge price for your red stone. A pigeon faints. Sell it, or keep it?

choice_ember_sell_high.narration: You name a bigger number. She names a smaller one. Back and forth you go, until a second pigeon faints. She pays double, and adds a brave whistle "for cheek, darlings."

scene_sold.narration: Madame Fenn pays you in a clanking purse and adds a lucky bead. "I never forget a good seller." The hum rolls away in her barrel.

scene_kept.narration: You close your hand around the warm stone. Madame Fenn sighs so hard her barrel rocks. The hum stays with you.

scene_provisions.narration: At the foot of the Outfitters' Steps, a sheeple grocer named Mrs. Tuft has her barge tied up. Her price tags are stuck in her wool. "One thing for the road, free," she says. "Food, a potion, or a light. Pick one."

scene_provisions_honey.narration: Mrs. Tuft packs six honeycakes in a tin. By the time the lid is on, there are five. Everybody has crumbs on their chin.

scene_provisions_sunbloom.narration: The sunbloom potion glows like a tiny sunrise. "For bumps, scrapes and grumps," says Mrs. Tuft. "Mostly grumps."

scene_provisions_mosslight.narration: The mosslight glows soft and green. "It likes to be talked to," says Mrs. Tuft. "Not sung to."

scene_provisions_stone.narration: Mrs. Tuft takes one look at the red stone, and every jar on her barge rattles. "Lovely," she says, not meaning it. She hands you a honeycake, so you will leave sooner.

scene_market.narration: At the top of the steps, a faun cobbler named Tobble Reedpipe sings the price of his quickfoot laces. Every verse goes higher. You can sing back, buy, or keep your coins.

scene_market_keep_coins.narration: You keep your coins. Tobble sings you down the steps, one key lower each step.

scene_market_spot_fakes.narration: Your kitsune points at the next stall. "Those are bootlaces painted yellow." Tobble is so grateful he gives you real quickfoot laces.

scene_market_fresh_start.narration: Tobble stops singing. "I had a fresh start too," he says. "I used to make boots for a duke." He sells you laces at last year's price.

scene_market_buy_outright.narration: You buy the best laces without asking the price. Tobble is so surprised he sings the price anyway, a whole key too high.

check_haggle.prompt: Sing the price back to Tobble, one key lower, without losing the tune

onSuccess.narration: You sing back, one key lower. Tobble is so delighted he sells you the laces at last week's price.

onFailure.narration: You sing back, but your note lands somewhere Tobble's song has never been. He loses his place and starts again from the top, twice. Somewhere in the muddle, money changes hands and something is wrapped in paper.

scene_laced.narration: The quickfoot laces go on. Right away, your feet want to be somewhere else, quickly.

scene_lace_tangle.narration: Your song and Tobble's get so tangled that he sells you a honeycake instead. Nobody knows how. It is a good honeycake, though.

scene_inn_full.narration: Back at the Empty Chair, the innkeeper is a stone troll named Flint, in a nightcap much too small. He has one cupboard bed left, and lots of people want it. "Earn it," he rumbles.

choices.label: Risk telling it over the noise

check_inn_story.prompt: Tell the red night so well a whole inn goes quiet

onSuccess.narration: You tell it all: the cherry-red sky, the gem-light falling, the seagull and its very surprised fish. The whole inn goes quiet. Flint wipes one eye with a dishcloth and hands you the cupboard key without a word.

onFailure.narration: Your story wanders off somewhere around the fish and never quite comes back. The prospectors laugh so kindly that Flint gives the cupboard to someone else and you the hayloft above the mules, which is warm, smells of apples, and is honestly nicer.

scene_inn_full_dishes.narration: There are three hundred supper bowls. You wash until your fingers wrinkle like raisins. At midnight Flint checks one bowl, says "Hm," and hands you the key.

scene_inn_full_selkies.narration: The selkie family hears your voices and comes thundering down the stairs. "You'll squash in with us," says the grandmother. The room is tiny, but warm.

scene_inn_full_outbid.narration: You open Madame Fenn's purse and name a number. Everyone else goes off to sleep in the stables. The cupboard is yours. It is a very expensive cupboard.

rest_empty_chair.narration: Cupboard, hayloft or squashed-up room, it is warm and dry. Through the wall, people argue happily about onions. Tomorrow the caravans leave.

scene_last_noodles.narration: At dawn you pass Mortar's noodle stall with your bags packed. He stirs one slow turn. "Going, then." There is time for one goodbye before the caravans leave.

choices.label: Leave a gift on the chair

scene_last_noodles_ask.narration: Mortar stirs one slow turn. Then another. "Longstride. Lantern wagon. Listens to the whole answer. Tell her Mortar sent you." That is the most he has said all week.

scene_last_noodles_gift.narration: You leave a button on the empty chair. Under it, someone has tied a songbird ribbon for whoever comes next. Mortar pretends not to see. He is smiling, very slowly.

scene_last_noodles_bowl.narration: Mortar ladles out the biggest breakfast of your lives, then pins his apron's thistle on you. "Strong noodles. Strong legs." A long stir. "Come back."

scene_last_noodles_listen.narration: Mortar holds the warm stone to his ear for a long time. "Sings," he says at last. "Like my grandma's pot, just before it boiled over."

scene_caravan_yard.narration: In the caravan yard, a centaur named Hesper Longstride is checking her lantern wagon. "I have room for one more crew," she says. "Tell me why you want to come."

scene_caravan_yard_banner.narration: The Longstride banner is taller than you, and the wind wants it badly. You hold it up anyway. "Front," says Hesper. "Don't drop it."

scene_caravan_yard_race.narration: A yeti crew bets you can't load a wagon faster. You finish while they argue about who goes first. Half of it is upside down. Hesper almost smiles.

scene_caravan_yard_guard.narration: "That wagon was robbed twice this week," says Hesper. You offer to guard it anyway. She hands you a long pole with a hook.

scene_caravan_yard_lift_wagon.narration: A wagon is stuck in the mud. You lift it out, along with a small faun who keeps eating breakfast. Hesper nods once.

scene_caravan_yard_mortar.narration: Hesper's ears swivel. "Mortar sent you? Mortar hardly talks to anybody." She nods once. From that troll, a name is as good as a letter.

check_signon.prompt: Tell a caravan master the truth and mean it

onSuccess.narration: Hesper listens to the whole answer, all the way to the end. Then she nods once, like a gate closing.

onFailure.narration: You get muddled halfway through and say "um" eleven times. Hesper is kind about it. Hesper is also busy.

scene_hired.narration: Hesper hands you a lantern pole. "Crew," she says. The wagons roll toward the North Gate.

scene_turnip_wagon.narration: "Cargo, then," says Hesper, kindly. You ride with the turnips. One sits in your lap like a cat. The wagons roll toward the North Gate.

scene_north_gate.narration: A big bell called the Leaving Bell hangs over the North Gate. Past it are green fields and, far away, Mount Red Sky. "Say goodbye however you like," says Hesper.

check_leaving_bell.prompt: Ring the Leaving Bell loud enough for the whole city

onSuccess.narration: You haul on the rope together. BONG. The bell is so loud that every gull in the harbor lifts off at once, and all over the Exchange, people you have never met stop and wave you goodbye.

onFailure.narration: You haul on the rope, and the rope hauls back. Up you go, dangling under the bell like the world's most surprised clapper. It rings anyway. The whole gate cheers, and Hesper waits, very patiently, for you to come down.

scene_north_gate_wave.narration: You wave, and the Exchange waves back. Tobble sings goodbye, three keys too high. Madame Fenn's barrel rolls along beside you. "Bring me something shiny, darlings!"

scene_north_gate_look.narration: You look north. Far away, Mount Red Sky glows red on top, like a candle somebody forgot to blow out. For a blink, it seems to look back.

scene_north_gate_tidewell.narration: There is Professor Tidewell, running beside the wagons. "Count every stone you see!" she shouts. "Write it down!" She throws you her napkin drawing, trips over a goose, and keeps waving.

rest_northbound.narration: That night the caravan camps in the first of the Sunward Fields, where the grass smells of honey and everybody's boots still smell of the city. Far to the north, the sky glows faintly red. Share out your things, patch each other up, and sleep.

variants.text: Your mail bags kept the letters dry.

interaction_quay_line.narration: Down on the quay, dockhands pass pear crates in a long line. You fill a gap. Not one pear drops, and the dockmaster gives you each a pear.

interaction_letters.narration: The letters are drifting toward the canal! A post clerk runs beside you with a ladle. Wait until a letter floats close, then grab it.

interaction.cue: Wait for the letter to float close, then grab it.

onSuccess.narration: You snatch the last letter just above the water. The clerk stamps it DELIVERED and hurries off.

onFailure.narration: The last letter splashes into the canal. The clerk fishes it out with her ladle and hurries off.

onAssisted.narration: The clerk grabs the last letter herself, stamps it DELIVERED, and hurries off.

interaction_jars.narration: Mrs. Tuft has a tray of jars for the top of the Outfitters' Steps, and you help carry it. The pickle jar rattles all the way up. At the top she counts them. "Good hands," she says.

interaction_lantern_pole.narration: On the way, a lantern pole snags a washing line. You hold the pole steady while Hesper unhooks it. Long underwear floats down onto a goat. "On to the North Gate," says Hesper.

scene_quay_wisps.narration: Down on the quay, the lamps are being lit, and the stone in your pocket hums louder. Two tiny wisps have followed it. They think it is a very small sun! They tangle in the lamp strings, and a ferry's rope comes loose. "Shoo them off!" cries the ferryman.

encounter_quay_wisps.narration: The wisps zip around the lamp strings, giggling and tugging. Shoo them off before the ferry drifts away.

scene_quay_wisps_shooed.narration: The wisps bob away over the water, giggling. The ferryman ties up his ferry and gives you a bright ribbon from his lamp string. "For the shooing."

scene_quay_wisps_scattered.narration: The wisps swirl until the quay is dizzy with sparkles. Then the ferryman bangs his kettle, and they pop away like bubbles. No ribbon, but everyone gets hot cocoa.

scene_caravan_yard_thornguard.narration: Your thornguard plants both boots by the lantern wagon. A pickpocket takes one look and leaves. "Steady," says Hesper, and hands over a long pole with a hook.

interaction_newcomer_load.narration: Everything goes on a carrying board, even a fishbowl. Raise or lower your side until it is level. The fish is counting on you.

interaction.cue: Level the carrying board before lifting the family's bags.

onSuccess.narration: You carry it all up to the inn, level as a table. The selkie children wave from their new window.

onFailure.narration: Halfway up the hill, a trunk pops open. Out pour a hundred knitted socks! Chasing them is the most fun anyone has had all week. The selkies get their room at the Empty Chair, socks and all.

onAssisted.narration: The grandmother steadies the fishbowl, and together you carry it all up to the inn.

interaction_post_routes.narration: Quill lays out three route cards. Share the clues and put the mail bags in order. She will leave them by the quay for more mail.

interaction.cue: Share the route cards and arrange the mail bags in loading order.
clues: The harbor bag loads before the valley bag.
The valley bag is between harbor and mountain.

onSuccess.narration: The bags are in order. Quill gives you a brave whistle and sets them by the quay.

onFailure.narration: You sort the letters beautifully, into all the wrong bags. A letter for a duke is now going to a duck. Quill sighs.

onAssisted.narration: Quill helps you read the cards. Together you set the bags in order, and she gives you a brave whistle.

interaction_checked_mail.narration: You pocket the stone. The letters flutter toward the mail bags you set out. A post clerk runs up with a ladle. Catch the bundle and pass it into the right bag.

interaction.cue: Catch the mail bundle and pass it to the checked bags.

onSuccess.narration: Every letter lands in the right bag. The clerk carries them off, delighted.

onFailure.narration: One letter escapes. The clerk scoops it up with her ladle and checks the bags herself.

onAssisted.narration: The clerk jumps in beside you, and together you fill the bags.

interaction_inn_account.narration: Flint makes room by the fire. Each hero tells a bit of the red night, or adds a sound.

choices.label: Add a gull or harbor sound

interaction_crew_introduction.narration: Each hero takes a turn: say why you are going north, or name a job you can do. A turnip rolls out of a wagon, as if it wants a job too.

interaction.cue: Each hero shares a reason to travel or a way to help.

options.label: Say why I want to go north
options.reaction: Hesper listens to your reason all the way to the end.

options.label: Offer a job I can help with
options.reaction: She writes your offered job on the crew list.

options.label: Ask Hesper what help she needs
options.reaction: Hesper explains a caravan job and leaves room for your answer.

onSuccess.narration: Hesper has heard everyone. She puts your party on the crew list.

onFailure.narration: You get muddled halfway through and say "um" eleven times. Hesper is kind about it. Hesper is also busy.

onAssisted.narration: Hesper asks one question at a time, and together you find your place on the crew list.

interaction_inn_account_response_sky.narration: Your part of the sky joins the story. Flint stops counting offers. The bed is yours.

interaction_inn_account_response_city.narration: Your memory of the city gets a nod from someone who was there. The bed is yours.

interaction_inn_account_response_sound.narration: The room answers your sound with another. Flint laughs into his dishcloth. The bed is yours.

voiceGuide.tone: gold-rush overture: bustling, funny, warm, a little mysterious about the red sky but never scary
forbidden: any one people owning or founding the Exchange
explaining what the gemstones really are

npcVoices.tidewell: Professor Marrow Tidewell, a selkie scholar with ink on both elbows; talks fast, draws on napkins, has been laughed out of better taverns and keeps going anyway
npcVoices.coralie_fenn: Madame Coralie Fenn, a merfolk gem-buyer in a barrel on wheels; calls everyone darlings, names enormous numbers cheerfully, never forgets a seller
npcVoices.tobble: Tobble Reedpipe, a faun cobbler who sings every price, going up a key each verse; delighted by anyone who sings back
npcVoices.hesper: Hesper Longstride, a centaur caravan master with a road-stitched sash; few words, listens to the whole answer, kind but busy
npcVoices.boggart: a rumor-selling boggart in a coat made of other coats; never says anything straight, always says it twice
npcVoices.lighthouse_keeper: a very old merfolk in a bathtub at the top of the lighthouse; firmly did not see anything
npcVoices.tour_guide: a centaur tour guide who loves the seventeen plaques and charges for every fact
npcVoices.mortar: Mortar, a stone troll noodle cook; stirs one full slow turn before answering anything, says very little, and means all of it
npcVoices.old_wick: Old Wick, a very old frogfolk lamplighter; croaks softly, wishes every lamp goodnight by name, knows the paths nobody else looks for
npcVoices.orange_captain: the yeti captain of the Sunny Disposition, an orange ship; cheerful, orange peel in his fur, pays every debt, mostly in oranges
npcVoices.postmaster_quill: Postmaster Quill, a griffin with glasses on a chain who runs the Griffin Post; squawks, loses count, insists it will all come out in the wash
npcVoices.courier_griffin: a young courier griffin, always hungry, bows with wings out to people it will remember
npcVoices.mrs_tuft: Mrs. Tuft, a sheeple grocer on a provision barge, wool full of price tags; everything comes in a jar; brisk and a little dry
npcVoices.selkie_grandmother: the grandmother of a selkie family just arrived for a fresh start; brisk, warm, decides things are settled and they are
npcVoices.innkeeper_flint: Innkeeper Flint, a stone troll who runs the Empty Chair inn in a very small nightcap; rumbles, folds his arms, secretly soft

interaction_quay_line.narration: A gap opens in the dockhands' pear-crate line. Catch and pass the crates along the quay. "Every pair of hands helps!" calls the dockmaster. His hat is sliding over his eyes.

interaction.cue: Catch the crate, then pass it down the line.

onSuccess.narration: Not one pear drops. The last crate reaches the top of the quay, and the dockmaster tips his hat so far forward it falls off. You each get a pear for the walk to the docks, and it is the best pear in the Exchange, which is saying something this week.

onFailure.narration: One crate slips, and a pear rolls all the way down the quay with a dockhand running after it. Everybody cheers when he catches it. You each get a slightly bruised pear for the walk to the docks.

onAssisted.narration: The dockmaster joins the gap in the line himself, and the crates go by smooth as a river. You each get a pear for the walk to the docks.

interaction_jars.narration: Mrs. Tuft loads a tray of jars for the Outfitters' Steps. Keep it level. One jar contains pickles; it would not mind a swim. The others would.

interaction.cue: Everyone lift or lower your side until the jars sit level, then carry the tray.

onSuccess.narration: Not a jar clinks. Mrs. Tuft counts them twice, finds every one, and writes a small tick in the air with her pencil. "Good hands," she says, which from a grocer is a lot. You carry the tray to the top of the steps.

onFailure.narration: The jars clink, tilt and slide, and one of them goes for a swim. Mrs. Tuft fishes it out with a net. "It was the pickled kind," she says. "It will not mind." You carry the rest of the tray to the top of the steps.

onAssisted.narration: Mrs. Tuft grabs one corner of the tray, and the jars settle at once. You carry it to the top of the steps together.

interaction_lantern_pole.narration: The lantern pole catches a washing line. Hold it steady while someone unhooks it. Long underwear flaps overhead. Hesper hopes it is not the new caravan flag.

interaction.cue: Friends hold the pole steady while someone unhooks the washing line.

onSuccess.narration: Click. The line comes free, and the long underwear floats down onto a very surprised goat. Not a lantern swings. Hesper nods once, and the wagons roll on to the North Gate.

onFailure.narration: The pole sways, the lanterns chime like bells, and the long underwear comes down on Hesper's head. She wears it with great dignity all the way to the North Gate.

onAssisted.narration: Hesper holds the pole steady herself and the line comes free. Not a lantern swings, and the wagons roll on to the North Gate.

interaction_inn_account.narration: Flint makes room beside the hearth. Each hero tells a little of the red night, or adds a sound to the story. Take your time. Flint has put his nightcap over the bidding bell.

interaction.cue: Each hero adds a memory or a sound from the red night.

options.label: Describe the red sky
options.reaction: Your part of the sky joins the story. Flint stops counting offers.

options.label: Tell what the city did
options.reaction: Your memory of the city gets a nod from someone who was there.

options.label: Add a gull or harbor sound
options.reaction: The room answers your sound with another. Flint laughs into his dishcloth.

onSuccess.narration: Flint thanks you for the story and gives you a warm place for the night.

onFailure.narration: Your story wanders off somewhere around the fish and never quite comes back. The prospectors laugh so kindly that Flint gives the cupboard to someone else and you the hayloft above the mules, which is warm, smells of apples, and is honestly nicer.

onAssisted.narration: Flint helps keep the story in order while you add your parts. He finds you a warm place for the night.
